Compiler Engines

Use the automatic compiler path and recognize a platform failure before rewriting correct C.

What you will learn

  • Explain TCC, the optional module and external fallback.
  • Match common execution errors to safe next steps.

Before you begin

A completed hello.c example. No engine-selector setup is required.

Read Auto as a policy

RUN starts with built-in TCC, uses the optional Clang module when available and falls back through compatible Termux when a compiler is blocked. The picker was removed; there is no current Settings Termux card. The Engines guide describes capabilities, not selectable controls.

Compiler coverage
ArchitectureBuilt-in pathImportant limit
arm64-v8aBundled TCCOptional Clang module also targets arm64
x86_64Bundled TCCCannot execute the arm64 module
32-bit ARM/x86No bundled TCCExternal compatibility is not guaranteed

Keep the first test small

probe.c

#include <stdio.h>
int main(void) { puts("compiler ready"); return 0; }

Terminal check

cc probe.c -o probe
./probe

Expected result

compiler ready

This conservative program separates toolchain startup from a complicated project. TCC is not a promise of all C11/C17 features or every desktop library. Keep -o last, and never overwrite CodeC’s cc frontend to imitate another compiler.

Three errors, three questions

  1. For Permission denied, ask whether Android policy or a noexec location blocks execution. Keep the source in a private CodeC project and read Output’s fallback guidance.
  2. For Exec format error, check CPU architecture against the executable. An arm64 binary cannot run on x86 or 32-bit ARM.
  3. For a missing runtime/library/tool, verify installation and the exact name. A compiler diagnostic about a semicolon is a source problem, not a reason to replace the environment.

An optional fallback walkthrough

Install compatible Termux0.109+ from F-Droid or its GitHub releases, linked in Install. In Termux, not CodeC, run:

Termux-only setup

echo "allow-external-apps=true" >> ~/.termux/termux.properties
termux-reload-settings
pkg update && pkg install clang

Grant CodeC the Android “Run commands in Termux environment” permission under Apps → CodeC IDE → Permissions → Additional permissions, then return and retry. Follow the Output instructions if device labels differ. Do not mix the two package repositories.

Try it yourself

  1. Run probe.c and record compiler/startup versus program output separately. Expected: the greeting or a specific actionable error, not a guessed diagnosis.
  2. Identify your device ABI from available device/log information. Compare it with the table without changing settings.
  3. Read a compiler diagnostic from a deliberately missing semicolon, then fix it. Expected: the tiny program runs again.

Common mistakes

  • There is no selector to switch to Termux manually.
  • A different APK download does not turn a 32-bit CPU into arm64.
  • Only follow the Termux setup when fallback is needed; first C should stay simple.
